title: Vanishing of an arbitrary module map at one affine chart stage
statement: Let I be a directed preorder, R a diagram of commutative rings and c an affine limit cone of Spec(R) [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-base-change]. Let f:X_i→Spec(R_i) be any morphism and i≤j≤k. Let U be an open cover of X_j with affine charts and fix a chart a. Put V=U pulled back to X_k. For quasi-coherent modules F,G on V.X a, with F of finite type and G of finite presentation [pqf-def-coherent], let δ:F→G. If the pullback of δ along the chart projection from the limit is zero, then for some l≥k its pullback along the canonical refinement chart map from l to k [def-pc-local-overlap-transitions] is zero. This concludes at one stage only; it has no transition system or coherence hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 01ZR (3), first proof (affine case), transported through the canonical chart pullback squares; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01ZR

proof.text: The map X_k→X_j is affine, being a base change of a map of spectra. Its inverse image W of the affine chart U.X a is affine. The structural map b:W→Spec(R_k) is consequently quasi-compact. Pull W back along the identity map of Spec(R_k); the first projection is an isomorphism. Transport F,G,δ to that pullback. Finite type, quasi-coherence and finite presentation are invariant under this isomorphism.

The limit chart is canonically isomorphic to W×Spec(R_k)c.pt: paste the chart pullback square with the base-change square for X. The same construction at l identifies the stage chart with W×Spec(R_k)Spec(R_l). The maps to W are the canonical cover projection and overlapRefinementHom respectively, because both pullback projections agree. On modules, pullbackComp and pullbackCongr give the corresponding natural comparisons. The tensor pullback defining moduleBaseChange and native pullback are naturally isomorphic by uniqueness of left adjoints to module pushforward; naturality preserves and reflects zero equations.

Apply finitePresentation_zero_map_descent to b with initial indices both k and to the transported source, target and map. The preceding limit comparison turns the hypothesis into the required limit-zero equation. Zero-map descent supplies l≥k. The stage comparison turns its conclusion into vanishing along the prescribed canonical refinement chart map. Zero modules and empty affine charts are covered without modification.

theorem finitePresentation_chart_map_zero_eventually
    {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)]
    (R : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u})
    (c : Cone (R.op ⋙ Scheme.Spec)) (hc : IsLimit c) [IsAffine c.pt]
    (i : I) {Xi : Scheme.{u}} (f : Xi ⟶ Spec (R.obj i))
    (j : I) (hij : i ≤ j)
    (U : (pullback f (Spec.map (R.map (homOfLE hij)))).OpenCover.{u})
    [∀ a, IsAffine (U.X a)] (a : U.I₀) (k : I) (hjk : j ≤ k)
    (F G : ((U.pullback₁ (overlapStageMap R f hij hjk)).X a).Modules)
    (hF_ft : F.IsFiniteType) (hF_qc : F.IsQuasicoherent)
    (hG_fp : G.IsFinitePresentation) (hG_qc : G.IsQuasicoherent)
    (δ : F ⟶ G)
    (hδ : (Scheme.Modules.pullback
      (Scheme.Cover.pullbackHom (U.pullback₁ (overlapStageMap R f hij hjk))
        (overlapLimitMap R c f (hij.trans hjk)) a)).map δ = 0) :
    ∃ (l : I) (hkl : k ≤ l),
      (Scheme.Modules.pullback
        (overlapRefinementHom U (overlapStageMap R f hij hjk)
          (overlapStageMap R f hij (hjk.trans hkl))
          (overlapStageMap R f (hij.trans hjk) hkl)
          (overlapStageMap_comp R f hij hjk hkl) a)).map δ = 0
